text:
Maya (CEO): quick follow-up for folks who missed the wins/losses section in today's all-hands. dropping a thread for clarifying q&a and action items about what customers actually told us they value
Liam (Head of Sales): field notes: one buyer said we won because our console flagged a quality regression before the competitor did. another buyer walked away because of hallucination risk on a core prompt set
Elena (Customer Success): +1. retention case study: customer stayed after we helped triage a production regression in 48h with clear root cause and rollback. they called that "the deciding factor"
Sam P. (VP Product): interesting. so observability + fast rollback beats raw perf in some cases. does CS have a written playbook we used there?
Elena (Customer Success): we used an internal checklist but it's not public. customers ask for "repro and rollback" examples in contracts or sales decks
Rohit (Solutions Eng): tech detail: we detected a tokenization change in their preprocess pipeline that increased effective sequence length and triggered cache churn. we shipped a hotfix and pinned a compatible model variant temporarily
Anya (PM): product question: should we add an "output-stability" card in Console that shows delta in distribution, top failing prompts, and recent rollbacks?
Sam P. (VP Product): yes. prioritize a small telemetry view: prompt-drift, token-length histograms, and a recent-regressions list. tie it to alerts and an on-call runbook
Liam (Head of Sales): Sales request: can we put a short line in our enterprise SOW about regression-support hours or a "regression credit"? buyers repeatedly asked for explicit remediation timelines
LegalBot: note: any SOW language promising timelines needs defined scope and exclusions. recommend offering a named add-on: "Regressions & Triage - up to 10 hours, one incident/week" with clear out-of-scope items
Elena (Customer Success): that would sell. customers also want reproducible evals and dataset lineage so they can verify fixes internally
Anya (PM): new artifact idea: "Regressions playbook" + a reproducible eval template (not just perf numbers) that Sales can show during procurement. includes sample prompts, diff tooling, and rollback steps
Rohit (Solutions Eng): include a short troubleshooting snippet for common causes: tokenization, prompt truncation, quantization mismatch, and model weight swaps. tiny code example: 
```
# quick check for token bloat
tokens = tokenizer.encode(prompt)
if len(tokens) > expected: warn('tokenization impact')
```
Sam P. (VP Product): also want to capture that we won some deals by offering A/B model rollouts and automatic fallback to a conservative variant when quality dips. can we expose that as a config?
Anya (PM): propose a toggle: model_rollout: { mode: a/b, fallback: conservative_variant, monitor: output_stability } in Dedicated and Console rollout UI
Liam (Head of Sales): that would address procurement fears. also request a 1-slide "how we manage regressions" Sales asset with bullets: detect, reproduce, rollback, SLA for triage hours
DocsBot: created docs/plays/regression-triage-playbook.md (draft) by Anya at 2212346755 :white_check_mark:
Maya (CEO): love the docs progress. logistics: who owns the add-on pricing and the slide?
Elena (Customer Success): CS can prototype the triage offering and pricing with Sales. we'll run a pilot for two customers this quarter to collect data
Sam P. (VP Product): Product will scope Console card + rollout config. Anya will own the playbook and the Sales slide. Rohit will provide the troubleshooting appendix and sample snippets
LegalBot: Legal will draft a short addendum template for the "Regressions & Triage" offering with clear caps and liability language. ping Legal when you have pricing numbers
Rohit (Solutions Eng): small ask: add a tiny telemetry flag in hosted responses that logs model-variant id and tokenizer version so we can correlate regressions quickly
Anya (PM): adding that to the scope. will propose a minimal telemetry schema that doesn't expose PII.
DeployBot: deployment note: docs/plays/regression-triage-playbook.md published (rev 0.1) by Anya at 2212346788 :white_check_mark:
Liam (Head of Sales): actionables for Sales: get two anonymized deal notes that referenced regressions/rollback as a win. I'll DM them to Anya and Elena
Maya (CEO): timeline check: can we get the Sales slide + draft SOW addendum + Console card spec by next Tuesday?
Anya (PM): yes. drafting now. ETA draft slide + playbook by Mon EOD, Console spec by Tue AM, Legal draft by Tue EOD
Sam P. (VP Product): we'll reprioritize a small sprint to add the output-stability card and rollout config. no big changes to other roadmap items
Elena (Customer Success): will update churn playbook to include regression triage as a retention lever and run the pilot with two customers
Maya (CEO): great work. please keep this thread updated with links to drafts. tag Anya for follow-ups. thanks everyone :sparkles:
